title: Inheritance in Kotlin
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of inheritance in kotlin using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates inheritance in kotlin.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Inheritance in Kotlin** as part of **Inheritance, Interfaces, and Polymorphism**. Use interfaces and inheritance when they express substitutability, and prefer composition when an object should contain or coordinate collaborators. Use the subtopics—Open Classes, Base and Derived Classes, Kotlin's Default Finality—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

items.title: Open Classes
items.text: Open Classes should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Inheritance is the default choice for sharing any behavior.
